purpose: Epoetin alfa is used to treat anemia, which means your body does not have enough red blood cells. It is commonly prescribed for people with chronic kidney disease, people receiving chemotherapy for cancer, or people who are on dialysis. It helps raise your red blood cell count so you feel less tired and weak.
how_it_works: Your kidneys normally make a natural protein called erythropoietin that tells your bone marrow to produce red blood cells. When your kidneys are not working well, or chemotherapy is affecting your body, not enough of this protein is made. Epoetin alfa is a man-made version of that same protein, and when injected, it signals your bone marrow to make more red blood cells, just like the natural version would.
common_side_effects: High blood pressure, headache, joint or muscle aches, nausea, swelling in your legs or arms, fever, and injection site reactions like redness or mild pain where the shot was given.
warnings: This medicine can increase the risk of serious problems like blood clots, stroke, heart attack, or even death, especially if your red blood cell count gets too high. It should not be used to completely eliminate the need for blood transfusions in surgery patients. If you have uncontrolled high blood pressure, tell your doctor before starting this medicine. Your doctor will check your blood regularly to make sure your red blood cell levels stay in a safe range.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given as an injection under the skin or into a vein. The dose depends on your condition, weight, and how your body responds. For kidney disease or dialysis, it is often given 3 times a week or once a week. For chemotherapy-related anemia, it may be given once a week or every 3 weeks. Your doctor will adjust the dose based on your blood test results.
